assistant.title: Let your personal assistants read your portrait
assistant.intro: Claude Code, Codex and other assistants with MCP support can connect to this WeClone. weclone_profile returns the domain summaries you approved, and weclone_search looks up entries by keyword or domain. All assistants share one token. The level and domains chosen below decide what they can read, and every call is logged with what it returned.

bots.title: Let chat bots call your clone
bots.intro: Bot platforms such as AstrBot and LangBot call the fine-tuned clone model through an OpenAI-compatible API. All bots share one token, entered as the platform's API key.
bots.tokenLife: A token stays valid once created, server restarts included, until you regenerate or revoke it.
bots.encrypted: Your data is encrypted. When a token is created, the data key is encrypted with it and stored in bots.sqlite3 on this machine. Bots unlock it with the token when they call, without you logging in. Anyone holding both the token and this file can decrypt all your data, so guard the token like a password. Changing your password doesn't affect the token. If you suspect a leak, regenerate it.
bots.noInference: The server hasn't loaded the clone model. Start it with weclone-cli server --inference before bots can call it.
bots.unused: No bot has used it yet
bots.noTokenHint: Create a token, then enter it as the API key on your bot platform.

setup.once: The token is shown only this once. On your bot platform, add an OpenAI-type model provider with this API base URL:
setup.model: Any model name works, for example gpt-3.5-turbo. The fine-tuned model doesn't call tools, so turn off tools and plugins on the platform. If the bot platform runs in Docker, replace 127.0.0.1 in the address with the host's address on the Docker network (for example 172.17.0.1) and start the server with --host set to that address.
